svg.title: Recurrent block data flow
svg.desc: One block (attention with a residual, FFN with a residual) applied R times to the same token state; the head reads every intermediate state during training (deep supervision) and the last one at inference; the parameter count does not change with R.
svg.text: RECURRENT BLOCK -- one block, applied R times
WHAT: 3812 parameters at every R (embedding 832, block 2096, norm and head 884); per token the block's parameters are touched R times.
deep supervision: loss = mean over r of masked_ce(head(norm(h_r)))
active parameters per token: R=1 2996 R=2 5092 R=3 7188 R=4 9284
WHY: depth normally costs parameters, one new layer per level. HRM and TRM show that reasoning depth can come from
applying one small block several times, so compute buys quality that storage does not have to pay for.
WHY: scoring every intermediate state (deep supervision) rewards each recurrence for improving the answer, so the
block learns a step that is worth repeating rather than a function that only works after exactly R uses.
HOW: u:recur_state applies the same global block inside repeat R (a parameter-bound count traces, finding F15);
chain(b, b) would copy the block (finding F3), so sharing is spelled by reusing one model value; u:recur_loss sums
the masked loss at every recurrence and divides by R; adam updates the one block through all R uses at once.
R=1 is exactly DN01 (tests/test_recur.mlpl asserts it); the sweep diagram shows what R=2..4 buy at the same parameters.
Each R trains in its own process (adam state is keyed by name, finding F22); the R=4 run is the recording the live demo replays.
